data.one_liner: A device simulator widget to speed up development for different devices on desktop and web.
data.what_it_does: It approximates how an app looks and behaves on various physical devices by simulating screen size, frames, notches, orientation, and safe areas inside desktop or web apps. It also includes a calibration screen to find correct values for custom devices.
use_when: You are developing a Flutter web or desktop app and want to preview mobile device layouts without changing windows.
You need to test how your app handles notches, home indicators, keyboard insets, and safe areas.
avoid_when: You are building mobile-only apps where you can readily use standard physical emulators or simulators.
You are not targeting web or desktop platforms for your development workflow.
strengths: Provides simulated frames, resolutions, orientations, and keyboard insets.
Supports custom device configurations and includes a calibration screen.
weaknesses: Requires the app to run as a desktop or web app to function as a simulator.
Not documented to work on mobile targets.
data.setup_notes: Wrap your root app with the DeviceSim widget, set useInheritedMediaQuery: true in your MaterialApp, and run the app on desktop or web.
